business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Clinical Workflow Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Gibraltar (British Overseas Territory) with Bermuda (British Overseas Territory) as the exempted company formation seat
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar and Bermuda)
UK–US FATCA Intergovernmental Agreement (extended to Gibraltar and Bermuda)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bermuda: Companies Act 1981 (as amended), Beneficial Ownership Act 2017, Proceeds of Crime Act 1997, Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018, Sanctions Act 2020. Gibraltar: Companies Act 2014 (including s.26 name clearance and Part 24 overseas companies), Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2017, Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, Sanctions Act 2019, Money Laundering Regulations 2019.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association and Statement of Activities
Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Declaration and AML/KYC Pack
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance officer of the registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorizing Gibraltar corporate service providers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening of all UBOs (holding 25% or more), directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury OFSI sanctions list, Gibraltar Sanctions Act 2019 list, EU consolidated sanctions (where applicable), and US OFAC SDN List. Individuals designated as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under the FATF definitions and Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 receive enhanced due diligence. The engaged registered agent must maintain a written AML risk assessment, evidence of screening timestamps, and a 5-year audit trail.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda: Registry of Companies e-Services (https://www.roc.gov.bm); Gibraltar: Companies House Gibraltar online portal (https://www.companieshouse.gi)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script. English is the official registration language in both Bermuda and Gibraltar. Non-Latin script names will be rejected unless accompanied by an English transliteration and a certified translation filed at the registry. The name of a Bermuda Exempted Company must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; a Gibraltar overseas company registration must use the same corporate name and an English version if applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Bermuda: within 21 days of a refusal the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Minister of Finance under Companies Act 1981 s.9(6), and thereafter to the Supreme Court of Bermuda. Gibraltar: within 14 days of a refusal the applicant may request the Registrar of Companies to issue a written statement of grounds and lodge an administrative appeal with the Companies Registry, followed by an appeal to the Financial Services Commission and ultimately the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under Companies Act 2014 s.34(8).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (as amended), ss. 3–20 (incorporation and registration), ss. 35–48 (share capital), ss. 102–116 (registered office), ss. 184–199 (directors); Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 and the Exempt Companies Regulations (exempt-company election status); Gibraltar Data Protection Act 2004 (medical-record data processing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar (Registrar of Companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-G1 (Application for Registration of a Company) with appended Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&AA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Gibraltar exempted company. The company may issue one or more shares with no par value; no escrow or blocked capital account is required by statute, but proof of subscribed funds or paid-up capital may be requested by the bank or EMI during account opening.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] It is RESOLVED that: (1) The subscribers' share subscription set out in the allotment schedule is approved and the shares are allotted to the named subscribers at par. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be established at [address], Gibraltar, and notice thereof shall be filed with the Registrar of Companies. (3) [Director 1], [Director 2] and [Director 3] are appointed as the first directors, and [Secretary] is appointed company secretary of the Company. (4) Each director and the secretary are authorised, jointly or singly, to complete, sign, file and submit all incorporation, tax status and banking documentation required to give effect to this resolution. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and reserved-name check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry – Name Availability Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one primary and two alternative names for availability check. The name must end in 'Limited' and must not contain restricted words such as 'Bank', 'Trust' or 'Insurance' absent a GFSC licence. Reserve the approved name for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Identification of proposed shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as misleading or restricted, receive the refusal grounds from the Registry, select an alternative available name or obtain the necessary GFSC consent, and re-submit the name search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare constitutional documents, share subscriptions and statutory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified Gibraltar corporate services provider and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, set out the subscribers' share subscription and allotment schedule, obtain consent-to-act forms from the first directors and company secretary, and notarise director and shareholder identity and address documents. Include an objects clause confirming software-as-a-service activities only, with no clinical-services delivery.
required_dossiers: Consents to act as director and secretary
Notarised passports and proof of residential address of each subscriber and director
Beneficial ownership statement for AML/CFT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any document is rejected on formality grounds, cure by executing corrected notarised duplicates and resubmitting; if a declaration is defective, file a statutory declaration of amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House – online incorporation filing e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CO-G1, the notarised M&AA, director and secretary consents, registered-office address and the government filing fee payment. Use the online portal for standard or expedited review; pay by bank wire or card.
required_dossiers: Final notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On query, the Registry issues a compliance note; respond through the same portal within 14 days, amend any offending clauses, pay any revised fee and await re-issuance of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and adopt first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies for certificate issuance; board of directors for governance resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the Certificate of Incorporation for exact name and company number; convene a board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution adopting the first board resolution covering registered office, share allotment and officer appointments. Execute share certificates and open statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Register of members and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is issued with a clerical error, apply to the Registrar for correction; if a board resolution fails for lack of quorum, circulate the resolution for unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File exempt-company election and commence bank or EMI onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar; licensed Gibraltar bank or electronic money institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the exempt-company election with the Commissioner of Income Tax within 30 days of incorporation, together with a declaration that the company will not transact with Gibraltar residents or carry on local trade. Use the election certificate for a low-risk EMI account under Gibraltar AML/KYC rules.
required_dossiers: Board resolution approving bank or EMI account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commissioner asks for evidence of non-resident ownership and no local-source income, provide the ownership schedule and a no-Gibraltar-trading business plan; if an EMI rejects the application, provide enhanced officer identity files and a privacy-compliance statement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office (Gibraltar), with corporate registration at Companies House Gibraltar; the Bermuda Exempted Company is simultaneously regulated by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 1981 and holds a Certificate of Exemption. No income or profits tax is imposed at the Bermuda level (zero-rate corporate tax jurisdiction), so the operative tax registration nexus for this structured trade is Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Stage 1 – Bermuda: file the exempted company incorporation and annual exemption declaration with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies and pay the annual government fee by 30 November; no Bermudian income tax registration or tax return filing is required because Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax on profits. Stage 2 – Gibraltar: register the Bermudian entity as an overseas company at Companies House Gibraltar (notice of place of business / branch), obtain the Gibraltar Companies House number, then file a company registration application with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office to obtain a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN); submit certified copies of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Exemption, memorandum and articles of association, a Gibraltar registered office address (service-provider office acceptable), and the intended date of commencement of trade. Stage 3 – Economic substance: identify the relevant activity (for EMR SaaS, the qualifying activity is Intellectual Property and/or Distribution and Service Centre) and file the Gibraltar annual economic substance return with the Income Tax Office. Stage 4 – UK VAT (if required): where B2C digital supplies are made to UK consumers, apply to HMRC under the Non-Established Taxable Person (NETP) procedure to obtain a UK VAT number; B2B supplies to UK VAT-registered medical clinics are subject to reverse charge and do not require supplier registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Bermuda or Gibraltar law; entity classification follows domestic corporate law, under which a Bermuda Exempted Company is an opaque limited-liability corporation. Available statutory elections and alignment mechanisms include: (i) election/designation as a Bermuda Exempted Company with an exemption permit; (ii) election under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act to compute capital allowances on qualifying plant, machinery and intellectual property, including the Gibraltar IP regime with a reduced effective rate on qualifying IP income under the modified nexus approach; (iii) voluntary election to treat the Gibraltar activity as a taxable permanent establishment of the Bermudian entity where this facilitates treaty access or substantiates economic substance; (iv) UK anti-hybrid notifications under CTA 2010 Part 6A / TIOPA 2010 to align the UK, Gibraltar and Bermuda tax characterisations and prevent deduction disallowance or double-dip mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No general VAT or GST applies in Gibraltar, which is outside the EU VAT area and applies only import duties and excise taxes to physical goods; UK VAT (Value Added Tax) at 20% is the relevant indirect tax for digital services supplied to UK consumers, while B2B supplies of EMR SaaS to UK VAT-registered medical clinics are outside the scope of UK VAT and subject to the customer's reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar: no VAT registration threshold is applicable because no VAT system exists; import duties arise regardless of turnover. UK: GBP 85,000 taxable turnover threshold applies to UK-established businesses, but a non-established supplier of digital/electronic services to UK consumers has no threshold and must register with HMRC from the first sale; B2B digital services to a UK VAT-registered customer are reverse-charged without supplier VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no fiscal e-invoicing clearance, no government digital stamping, no API real-time clearance, and no electronic invoicing mandate; conventional commercial e-invoicing is accepted. If the Bermudian/Gibraltar operator registers for UK VAT, HMRC requires Making Tax Digital (MTD) compliance, namely digital record-keeping and VAT return submission via MTD-compatible software over HMRC APIs; no real-time clearance or stamping applies. For UK public-sector e-invoicing, the PEPPOL network is required, but it is not relevant to private medical-clinic SaaS sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar has no VAT, so no Gibraltar export zero-rating exists and no refund mechanism is engaged for exported services. For UK VAT purposes, zero-rating of physical goods exported from the UK is available only where the supplier holds commercial export evidence (customs declaration and bill of lading/air waybill) obtained within three months and retained for six years. The medical-clinic EMR SaaS subscription is a cross-border digital service: B2B supplies to UK VAT-registered clinics are outside the scope of UK VAT (reverse charge), and B2C digital supplies are taxed at the place of consumption, so no export zero-rating claim is made for the software itself; any hardware bundled with the service could be separately zero-rated subject to the same evidence rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (UK SAD C88 / CDS Goods Departure Message; for the pure SaaS service no customs declaration is required, but it is mandatory for any physical hardware exports supporting the EMR installation)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or CMR consignment note for land freight) as proof of physical departure from the UK/Gibraltar export territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/statement confirmation evidencing receipt of the subscription consideration from the UK medical clinic customer
Commercial invoice and executed SaaS/subscription agreement with the UK clinic setting out the supply nature and the zero-rated or reverse-charged VAT treatment
Digital service delivery evidence (login credentials, cloud service logs, data-centre delivery receipt or go-live certificate) demonstrating that the cross-border service was actually rendered
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar: the Income Tax Office may raise assessments, amend returns and impose interest plus penalties of up to 100% of the tax under-charged for negligent or fraudulent conduct; assessment time limits are generally six years, extended to 21 years for fraud or wilful default. UK: HMRC audits zero-rating via post-clearance checks under VAT Notice 703 and may retrospectively claw back wrongly claimed zero-rating with interest; civil penalties under Schedule 24 Finance Act 2007 reach 100% of the potential lost VAT for deliberate and concealed inaccuracy, and criminal prosecution for VAT evasion (including fraudulent export schemes) carries imprisonment of up to seven years with unlimited fines; HMRC assessments may be made within four years for careless errors and up to 20 years for deliberate concealment. For the Bermuda Exempted Company, abusive use of the exemption status could result in cancellation of the Certificate of Exemption and fines under Bermuda's Companies Act 1981, while artificial Gibraltar/Bermuda routing of UK-derived SaaS profits may additionally be counteracted by the UK diverted profits tax (25%) or anti-hybrid mismatch rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the integrated financial regulator for banks and electronic money institutions; the Bank of England as the ultimate monetary authority for the Gibraltar pound (GIP), which is issued by the Government of Gibraltar through the Commissioner of Currency. For any Bermuda-resident banking or fiduciary arrangements, the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) applies separately; however, the operational treasury nexus of this structure is Gibraltar, so GFSC rules govern the account relationships and FX activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: GIP is pegged at par to GBP and is fully convertible; neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda maintains exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Medical-clinic EMR SaaS subscription receipts in GBP, EUR or USD may be freely received, retained and converted offshore. Capital account transactions (inbound share capital, intercompany loans, profit distributions to the Bermuda parent) are unrestricted and require no prior central bank approval. Profit remittance from Gibraltar to Bermuda is subject only to standard transfer-pricing documentation for the Gibraltar branch or permanent establishment and to anti-money-laundering record-keeping; Bermuda levies no withholding or remittance tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. No statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Gibraltar or Bermuda. SaaS export receipts may be held indefinitely in any freely convertible currency. The only affirmative obligations are GFSC anti-money-laundering record retention (five years) and accurate reflection of all receivables in the audited financial statements filed with the Gibraltar Companies Registry.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. UK-regulated EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex) will generally onboard a Bermuda Exempted Company operating from Gibraltar, but only after enhanced due diligence requiring full UBO disclosure, evidence of economic substance in Gibraltar and a primary transactional account with a GFSC-regulated bank. Gibraltar-licensed EMIs are permitted under the Financial Services (Electronic Money) Act, yet no Gibraltar EMI currently accepts an offshore tax-exempt vehicle without a domestic banking anchor. EMIs should therefore be used exclusively as low-value collection gateways for SaaS receipts and never as primary treasury reservoirs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: An in-person interview of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner is generally mandatory for the first onboarding of an offshore exempted company at all three tier-1 Gibraltar banks. Remote video onboarding is available only at Jyske Bank (Gibraltar) Ltd where the signatory is physically present in the UK or EU, all corporate documents are apostilled, and a Gibraltar-licensed professional introducer provides a formal attestation. A Bermuda-based director cannot be boarded in absentia; the company must maintain at least one Gibraltar-resident director who can attend the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore entity (Bermuda Exempted Co) flagged as preferential tax regime risk under GFSC AML guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar of Companies Certificate of Good Standing; latest certificate of compliance; complete ownership chain with UBO registry extract; Gibraltar economic substance declaration; evidence of active trading comprising office lease, local payroll, board minutes and audited financial statements demonstrating operating rather than treasury activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between incorporation domicile (Bermuda) and claimed operational jurisdiction (Gibraltar).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar registered-office agreement and business licence; executed UK/EU medical-clinic client contracts; supplier invoices and cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure) agreements; statutory annual audited accounts filed at the Gibraltar Companies Registry; and a board resolution confirming the Gibraltar branch as the principal place of management and control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face signatories and cross-border capital injection originating from Bermuda.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled board resolutions and powers of attorney; certified passports of all directors and UBOs; reference letter from a Bermuda-licensed bank or a licensed fiduciary introducer; 24-month bank statements evidencing source of wealth for the injected capital; and a completed GFSC-compliant prospective-client risk questionnaire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control approval is required. Recommended routing: Bermuda parent instructs its correspondent bank to transfer via SWIFT MT103 to Jyske Bank (Gibraltar) Ltd, with field 70 (Remittance Information) reading 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — GB__GI__BM_EXEMPTED_CO'; ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity-related investment) should be populated, or UK purpose code 'P0001' (intercompany transfer) where the counterparty is an affiliated group entity. Because GIP is pegged at par with GBP, the capital may be credited directly in Sterling with no conversion requirement. Verification bundle: board resolution allotting the shares, Bermuda share register excerpt, share certificate, certificate of incumbency, and UBO source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SaaS vendor settlements (cloud infrastructure, software licensing, contractor and licence fees) clear via: SWIFT MT103 with UETR for cross-border payments; SEPA Instant for Euro disbursements; CHAPS for same-day Sterling above GBP 1 million; and Faster Payments for domestic Sterling below GBP 1 million. For high-value infrastructure procurement exceeding GBP 250,000, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700, ICC UCP 600) confirmed by a UK clearing bank is the mandated rail; disbursement requires board-approved supplier onboarding and invoice matching under GFSC AML record-keeping rules. Dividend or profit distributions to the Bermuda parent are executed by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'DIVIDEND / PROFIT DISTRIBUTION (DIVD)' plus board minutes and audited accounts; no Gibraltar or Bermuda withholding applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts in GBP/EUR and GBP/USD with tenor up to 12 months under a board-approved ISDA or local master agreement.
Vanilla European FX options and zero-premium collars (GBP call / EUR put) purchased exclusively from tier-1 counterparties.
Cross-currency swaps in EUR/USD or GBP/EUR matched against SaaS receivable and vendor payable profiles.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on USD/GBP or USD/GIP, permitted only with a documented underlying receivable exposure and a minimum notional of EUR 1 million; not recommended given the GIP-GBP fixed parity, but allowed by Gibraltar banks where invoice currency mismatch is proven.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Confirmation Statement confirming registered particulars and statutory registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately GIP 100 (USD 130) on the company and each defaulting officer; continued default for 3 months after the Registrar's notice exposes the company to administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing or Audit Exemption Declaration (filed with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private exempted/small company: no later than 9 months after the financial year-end; the audit-exemption declaration accompanies the Annual Return filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver accounts or the exemption declaration attracts a fine of up to GIP 1,000 (USD 1,300) plus continuing daily default penalty; continued default after notice may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Self-Assessment) for the tax-resident/exempt company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar Income Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 November following the close of the tax year (e.g., 31 December 20X0 returns due 30 November 20X1); extended filing may be granted by the Commissioner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fixed penalty up to GIP 1,000 (USD 1,300), daily continuing penalties, interest on unpaid tax, and criminal sanctions for false statements; nil/exempt companies must still submit a return unless formally exempted in writing.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Tax Return Form CT-100 (Income Tax Act 2010, s 52) submitted online via the Gibraltar Tax Office 'iTax' portal at https://itax.gibraltar.gov.gi. Non-resident companies electing the PE filing path use Form CT-100NR.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual; advance payment quarterly when the annual tax liability exceeds GIP 100,000
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be delivered before the later of 31 January following the year of assessment (1 July to 30 June) and 12 months after the end of the accounting period. Tax is due on the filing date; estimated or advance payments are due on 30 June and 31 December for assessment periods.
